verdict.rationale: Letta is a conversational agent product, so natural-language operation is its core interaction model. Users can teach memory in plain language ("/remember always use pnpm in this repo", with the agent deciding where the lesson belongs), mention agents in Slack to have them do real work, schedule recurring prompts, have agents open PRs or sweep bug reports, and even have the agent modify its own runtime via mods. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of natural-language operation, and evidence that product administration and settings, not just agent tasks, can be driven by plain language rather than slash commands or keybindings.
